newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax resumes talks with Staples.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax resumes talks with Staples.

text.p: OfficeMax has resumed talks to acquire dozens of stores from Staples Inc., sources close to the talks said Tuesday, which could clear the way for government approval of Staples' $4 billion merger with rival office supply chain Office Depot Inc.

If the negotiations for Staples to sell stores to OfficeMax are successful, which could take weeks, the deal could lead to government approval of the Staples-Office Depot merger by the Federal Trade Commission.

The OfficeMax negotiations had broken down over a dispute about which stores would change hands, with money also an issue. In the absence of a divestiture agreement, the FTC rejected the Staples-Office Depot merger.

The FTC had required a divestiture of 62 stores by Staples to do the 1,000-plus store deal. Staples took the proposal to OfficeMax, which accepted 52 of the stores but wanted 20 others of its own choosing.

There was a second problem: Staples wanted $150 million to $160 million for the mix of stores it was offering, while OfficeMax was willing to pay only $100 million for the more than 70 stores it wanted to purchase.
Given those problems, the negotiations broke down and the FTC acted.
